claims.statement: The relocated module offers reusable small demonstrations of ordered profile splicing, substring filtering, scalar halving and callback sequencing, with an actual incompatible-colour rejection. Its scope is teaching; it supplies no paid-model performance evidence.

findings.statement: The teaching partial_compose preserves profiles in the tested unary associativity/unit cases, but resulting OperadOp records differ through name/id construction. Its unrestricted tree also accepts a child with the wrong colour. The associativity-named retained test checks only tree shape. No equality quotient, evaluator or well-formedness proof closes that gap.
findings.recommended_action: State profile-only semantics, or add a typed tree representation/equality and test genuine operad laws before reusing it as a workflow validator.

findings.statement: The teaching contraction verifier accepts a jump from0 to100 and accepts1 to0.9 when its declared contraction factor is0.5. It compares adjacent values above a threshold and does not check its advertised Lipschitz bound or finite nonnegative norm inputs.
findings.recommended_action: Admit the norm domain and verify the stated factor-bound for each transition, with explicit zero/nonfinite cases.

findings.statement: The teaching receipt emitter accepts empty role names and returns the same mutable dictionary stored in its history. Changing the returned authority_effect also changes stored history while retaining the old digest. The field and hash alone do not enforce immutable non-authoritative custody.
findings.recommended_action: Keep this a simulated receipt or use immutable records with verified bindings and independent custody. Do not count a stored digest as authenticated inspection.

controls.limit: No evaluation semantics or declared equality quotient is supplied; profile-splicing agreement is a narrower property than operation equality.
This unrestricted toy tree has no well-formedness verifier. It is not a production tree bypass.
Thresholded adjacent comparison is not a nonnegative finite-norm or specified Lipschitz-factor certificate.
Local dictionary emitter only; a separate hash verifier could detect alteration but none is applied here.
